answer: Run each epoch's rewards through a saffron filter: compare every answer against the nebula of that epoch's submissions and split one payout among near-duplicates, so a sybil farm cloning a single good answer across a hundred identities divides one reward a hundred ways. The signal that pays is originality — only genuinely distinct work earns in full — while cloning still costs the farm a fee and an attestation slot per identity. Duplication becomes self-defeating: the farm must do real, varied work per identity, exactly the cost it tried to dodge.
